stem: Which statement explains an advantage of a bone in the macaw’s tongue that the hornbill does NOT need?

options.label: A
options.text: It helps macaws catch and chew small mammals and crustaceans.

options.label: B
options.text: It helps macaws break open and eat tropical fruits and nuts.

options.label: C
options.text: It helps macaws make large holes in trees to reach insects to eat.

options.label: D
options.text: It helps macaws swallow whole prey.

visual_elements: Table comparing Great Hornbill and Macaw: Great Hornbill has long, curved beak, no bone in tongue, long toes for grasping, mostly black-colored body, omnivore (insects, small animals, soft fruits). Macaw has short, curved beak, tongue has bone, long toes for grasping, bright, colorful body, herbivore (fruits, nuts, berries, seeds).
Images of Great Hornbill and Macaw perched on branches.
